text: In the first century, in Galilee beside its great lake, Mary Magdalene lived in the time of Jesus. Her name tells us where she came from: Magdala, a town beside the lake. The Gospel says Jesus had freed Mary from great suffering. Mary was among the women who traveled with Jesus and the twelve apostles. She helped support their work. She listened, stayed close, and became his disciple.
sentences: In the first century, in Galilee beside its great lake, Mary Magdalene lived in the time of Jesus.

Mary was among the women who traveled with Jesus and the twelve apostles.
She helped support their work.
She listened, stayed close, and became his disciple.

text: People gathered to hear Jesus speak about the kingdom of God. Some brought questions. Some carried worries. Mary traveled with the group, learning from him and helping as they went. Following Jesus did not mean standing still in one place. There were roads and villages, meals to share, and people to care for.
sentences: People gathered to hear Jesus speak about the kingdom of God.

Some carried worries.
Mary traveled with the group, learning from him and helping as they went.

There were roads and villages, meals to share, and people to care for.

text: Then came a terrible day in Jerusalem. Jesus was crucified. Mary Magdalene stood near the cross with other women who loved him. She could not make that day safe or easy, but she was there. Mary had companions, too; she was not the only person who mourned Jesus. If this part is hard to hear, you can talk with someone who cares for you.

text: After Jesus died, his body was placed in a tomb. A large stone closed its entrance. The Sabbath was a day of rest. Then, early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary went to the tomb. Mary found that the stone had been moved. The entrance was open. She thought Jesus' body had been taken away, and she ran to tell Peter and the other disciple.

A large stone closed its entrance.
The Sabbath was a day of rest.

text: Peter and the other disciple hurried to the tomb and looked inside. They saw the burial cloths, but did not find Jesus' body. They went home. Mary stayed outside, crying. She bent to look into the tomb and saw two angels. They asked why she was weeping. Mary answered that her Lord had been taken away, and she did not know where he was. Then she turned and saw a man standing nearby. She thought he was the gardener.

Then she turned and saw a man standing nearby.
She thought he was the gardener.

text: The man asked why she was weeping and whom she was looking for. Mary asked him to tell her where Jesus had been laid, if he had carried him away. Then Jesus called her by name. Mary! She turned toward him and called him Rabbouni, which means Teacher. The person she had been searching for was there before her, alive. Her sorrow became joy.
sentences: The man asked why she was weeping and whom she was looking for.

text: Jesus gave Mary a message for the others. He was going to his Father and their Father, to his God and their God. Mary went to the disciples and told them she had seen the Lord. She also told them what Jesus had said. The woman who had come to the tomb in tears now carried the news of his resurrection.

Mary went to the disciples and told them she had seen the Lord.

text: Long afterward, Christians remembered Mary Magdalene as the "apostle of the apostles." That title honors the message she brought to them. The Church celebrates her feast on July 22. Her name belongs in the Easter story: Mary.
sentences: Long afterward, Christians remembered Mary Magdalene as the "apostle of the apostles." That title honors the message she brought to them.
The Church celebrates her feast on July 22.
Her name belongs in the Easter story: Mary.

text: The news Mary carried was not that the tomb was empty. She had seen Jesus alive. The disciple who had stood near the cross became a messenger of his resurrection. Christians still hear her witness when they read John's Gospel. Jesus called her by name, and she went to tell the others.
sentences: The news Mary carried was not that the tomb was empty.

Jesus called her by name, and she went to tell the others.

title: Points of reflection
points: What changed for Mary when Jesus called her by name?
With a parent or caregiver, read John, chapter 20, verses 11 through 18. Listen for the moment when Mary recognizes Jesus and the message he gives her.
Today, ask someone in your family about one good thing that happened to them. Give them time to answer.
Jesus, help us recognize your love and make room for the people you place beside us. Amen.
